1755.us: In Britain’s American colonies, French and Native forces routed General Braddock’s army near Fort Duquesne in July; young George Washington survived. In November an earthquake shook Boston.
1755.latam: Guaraní mission villages fought Spanish and Portuguese troops enforcing a 1750 border swap. Pombal’s Portugal banned enslaving Amazon peoples and founded a monopoly company for Grão-Pará and Maranhão.
1755.europe: Lisbon’s 1 November earthquake shocked the continent. In London, Samuel Johnson published his Dictionary of the English Language, while Britain and France drifted toward the Seven Years’ War.
1755.russia: Empress Elizabeth founded Moscow University in January, a project of scholar Mikhail Lomonosov and her favourite Ivan Shuvalov. In the Urals, the mullah Batyrsha led a Bashkir uprising.
1755.mideast: Sultan Osman III completed Istanbul’s Nuruosmaniye Mosque, an early Ottoman Baroque landmark. In Morocco, the Lisbon tsunami struck the coast, and a separate November quake hit Meknes.
1755.africa: In Ethiopia, Emperor Iyasu II died and his son Iyoas I took the throne. At the Dutch Cape, a smallpox epidemic struck colonists, slaves and Khoikhoi.
1755.india: British and Peshwa forces took the sea fort of Suvarnadurg from the naval chief Tulaji Angre in April. In Delhi, Mughal emperor Alamgir II was a puppet of his vizier Imad-ul-Mulk.
1755.china: Qianlong’s armies took Ili, heart of the Dzungar Mongol state, but their ally Amursana soon rebelled. In Japan, a cold, wet summer brought the Hōreki famine to the northeast.

1789.us: George Washington was sworn in as first president at New York’s Federal Hall on 30 April. In September Congress sent the states the amendments that became the Bill of Rights.
1789.latam: In Brazil, Portuguese officials uncovered the Minas Gerais independence plot and arrested its leader, Tiradentes. In French Saint-Domingue, planters and free people of colour pressed rival claims in revolutionary Paris.
1789.europe: Beyond France’s revolution, the Austrian Netherlands rose in the Brabant Revolution in October. In Britain, George III recovered from mental illness, ending the Regency Crisis.
1789.russia: Catherine the Great was at war with both Sweden and the Ottomans. General Alexander Suvorov, with Austrian allies, routed Ottoman armies at Focșani and Rymnik, in today’s Romania.
1789.mideast: Sultan Abdul Hamid I died in April, and the reform-minded Selim III took the Ottoman throne amid a losing war with Russia and Austria. Austria captured Belgrade in October.
1789.africa: In Dahomey, King Kpengla died and his son Agonglo took the throne after a palace struggle. In Sierra Leone, Temne ruler King Jimmy burned Granville Town, home to Black settlers from London.
1789.india: In December, Tipu Sultan of Mysore attacked the Travancore Lines, defences of a British ally, setting off the Third Anglo-Mysore War. Governor-General Cornwallis was reworking Bengal’s land revenue system.
1789.china: In January, Vietnam’s Tây Sơn leader Nguyễn Huệ routed a Qing army at Hanoi. In Japan’s north, Ainu on Kunashir and the Menashi coast rose against Japanese traders and were crushed.

1790.us: The first census counted about 3.9 million people, and Rhode Island became the last original state to ratify the Constitution. Benjamin Franklin died in Philadelphia in April.
1790.latam: Workers paving Mexico City’s main square unearthed the Aztec Sun Stone and a statue of Coatlicue. In Saint-Domingue, Vincent Ogé led a failed revolt demanding votes for free men of colour.
1790.europe: Paris celebrated the Bastille’s fall with the Festival of the Federation, and a new law made priests state employees. In London, Edmund Burke published Reflections on the Revolution in France.
1790.russia: Russia made peace with Sweden at Värälä in August. Writer Alexander Radishchev attacked serfdom in print and was condemned to death, commuted to Siberian exile.
1790.mideast: Under Prussian pressure, Austria agreed at Reichenbach in July to return its Ottoman conquests. In December, Russian troops stormed the Danube fortress of Izmail, killing most of its garrison.
1790.africa: In Madagascar, King Andrianampoinimerina was uniting the Merina highlands from Ambohimanga. James Bruce published his account of travelling through Ethiopia to the source of the Blue Nile.
1790.india: The Third Anglo-Mysore War began, with the East India Company, the Marathas and Hyderabad allied against Tipu Sultan. Tipu checked the first British invasion of Mysore.
1790.china: Opera troupes from Anhui came to Beijing for the Qianlong Emperor’s 80th birthday, seeding Peking opera. Japan’s shogunate banned “heterodox” Confucian teaching at its official academy.

1796.us: George Washington published his Farewell Address and stepped aside. John Adams narrowly beat Thomas Jefferson for president, and Tennessee became the 16th state.
1796.latam: In Saint-Domingue, Toussaint Louverture rescued French governor Laveaux from a coup and was named lieutenant governor. Spain joined France against Britain in October, exposing its colonies to British attack.
1796.europe: Newly married to Joséphine, Napoleon Bonaparte led France’s Army of Italy to victories at Lodi and Arcole. In December a French fleet tried and failed to land troops in Ireland.
1796.russia: Catherine the Great died in November, and her son Paul I succeeded her. Paul recalled an army invading Persia and freed the Polish rebel leader Tadeusz Kościuszko.
1796.mideast: Agha Mohammad Khan was formally crowned shah, founding Iran’s Qajar dynasty, and seized Mashhad from the last Afsharid ruler. Selim III kept building his European-style Nizam-ı Cedid army.
1796.africa: Scottish explorer Mungo Park reached the Niger River at Ségou in July. At the Cape, seized by Britain in 1795, a Dutch fleet sent to retake it surrendered at Saldanha Bay.
1796.india: Britain seized the Dutch forts of coastal Ceylon, taking Colombo in February. In Pune, Baji Rao II became Maratha Peshwa after months of court intrigue.
1796.china: The Qianlong Emperor formally handed the throne to his son Jiaqing but kept real power. The White Lotus Rebellion broke out in central China, lasting until 1804.

1811.us: In January, hundreds of enslaved people rose near New Orleans in the German Coast uprising. In November Governor Harrison fought Tecumseh’s confederacy at Tippecanoe, and in December the New Madrid earthquakes began.
1811.latam: Venezuela declared independence from Spain on 5 July. In Mexico, rebel priest Miguel Hidalgo was captured and executed, while Paraguay threw off Spanish rule in May.
1811.europe: In Britain, the Prince of Wales became Regent for his ailing father, George III. In Portugal, Masséna’s starving French army retreated from Wellington’s Lines of Torres Vedras.
1811.russia: Alexander I opened the Tsarskoye Selo Lyceum, where young Alexander Pushkin was among the first pupils. On the Danube, Kutuzov trapped and defeated an Ottoman army near Ruse.
1811.mideast: In March, Egypt’s Ottoman governor Muhammad Ali had the Mamluk leaders massacred at the Cairo Citadel. Later that year he sent an army against the first Saudi state in Arabia.
1811.africa: At the British-held Cape, Colonel John Graham’s troops began driving Xhosa communities east of the Fish River in December. Black American shipowner Paul Cuffe visited Freetown to explore resettlement.
1811.india: Governor-General Lord Minto sent an Indian army that seized French-controlled Java in August. In Punjab, Ranjit Singh kept building his Sikh empire.
1811.china: In Korea, Hong Gyeong-nae launched a major revolt in the northwest in December. Japanese guards seized Russian captain Vasily Golovnin on Kunashir, holding him for two years.

1830.us: President Andrew Jackson signed the Indian Removal Act in May, paving the way for the Trail of Tears. Joseph Smith published the Book of Mormon and founded his church.
1830.latam: Gran Colombia broke apart as Venezuela and Ecuador left, and Simón Bolívar died near Santa Marta in December. Uruguay adopted its first constitution.
1830.europe: France’s July Revolution replaced King Charles X with Louis-Philippe, and Belgians rose against Dutch rule in August. In England, farm workers smashed threshing machines in the Swing Riots.
1830.russia: In November, Polish cadets in Warsaw rose against Tsar Nicholas I, starting the November Uprising. A cholera epidemic reached Moscow, and quarantine trapped Pushkin on his Boldino estate.
1830.mideast: France landed troops in Ottoman Algeria in June and took Algiers on 5 July, beginning 132 years of French rule. In February the great powers recognised Greek independence.
1830.africa: Brothers Richard and John Lander traced the Niger River to its delta, settling where it met the sea. Dingane, who had killed Shaka in 1828, ruled the Zulu kingdom.
1830.india: Reformer Ram Mohan Roy sailed for Britain as the Mughal emperor’s envoy, a year after Lord Bentinck outlawed sati, the burning of widows, in Bengal.
1830.china: In Japan, about five million people joined the okage mairi, a mass pilgrimage to the Ise shrines. In Qing China, silver flowed out as opium imports kept rising.

1845.us: James K. Polk became president, Florida became a state, and Texas joined in December. Frederick Douglass published his Narrative, and the phrase “manifest destiny” entered print.
1845.latam: Britain and France blockaded the River Plate against Argentina’s ruler Juan Manuel de Rosas, battling his forces at Vuelta de Obligado. Mexico broke off relations with the US over Texas.
1845.europe: Potato blight struck Ireland in September, beginning a famine that would kill about a million people. Sir John Franklin sailed to find the Northwest Passage and never returned.
1845.russia: In the Caucasus, Mikhail Vorontsov’s army captured Imam Shamil’s stronghold at Dargo but lost thousands on the retreat. The Russian Geographical Society was founded in St Petersburg.
1845.mideast: In French Algeria, troops under Colonel Pélissier suffocated hundreds of villagers sheltering in the Dahra caves. In Ottoman Mount Lebanon, Druze–Maronite fighting flared again.
1845.africa: British and French warships shelled Tamatave after Madagascar’s Queen Ranavalona I ordered foreign traders to obey local law or leave. Her forces drove off the landing party.
1845.india: In December the Sikh Khalsa army crossed the Sutlej, starting the First Anglo-Sikh War, with bloody battles at Mudki and Ferozeshah. Denmark sold Tranquebar and its other Indian posts to Britain.
1845.china: Shanghai’s new Land Regulations set aside a British settlement, seed of the later International Settlement. In Japan, Abe Masahiro took charge of the shogun’s senior council.

1848.us: Gold was found at Sutter’s Mill in California, and a February treaty ending the Mexican War handed the US a vast territory. The Seneca Falls Convention demanded women’s rights.
1848.latam: Mexico confirmed the loss of about half its territory, including Texas, to the United States. France abolished slavery in Martinique and Guadeloupe, and Maya rebels in Yucatán’s Caste War nearly took Mérida.
1848.europe: Revolutions shook France, the German states, the Austrian Empire and Italy. Marx and Engels published The Communist Manifesto, and Louis-Napoléon Bonaparte was elected French president.
1848.russia: Nicholas I kept the revolutions out, sending troops to crush uprisings in Moldavia and Wallachia. A cholera epidemic killed hundreds of thousands across the empire.
1848.mideast: In Iran, 17-year-old Naser al-Din Shah took the throne as the Babi movement spread. In Egypt, Ibrahim Pasha replaced his ailing father Muhammad Ali but died within months.
1848.africa: Joseph Jenkins Roberts became the first president of independent Liberia. In southern Africa, Governor Harry Smith annexed the lands beyond the Orange River and defeated Boers at Boomplaats.
1848.india: Lord Dalhousie arrived as governor-general and annexed Satara using the “doctrine of lapse”. A revolt at Multan in April grew into the Second Anglo-Sikh War.
1848.china: In Guangxi, Hong Xiuquan’s God Worshipping Society was gaining followers, three years before the Taiping Rebellion. In Japan, American Ranald MacDonald slipped ashore and taught English to Nagasaki interpreters.

1858.us: Abraham Lincoln and Stephen Douglas debated slavery seven times in their Illinois Senate race, which Douglas won. Minnesota became the 32nd state.
1858.latam: Mexico’s Reform War began in January, pitting Benito Juárez’s liberals against a conservative government in Mexico City. Juárez set up his government in Veracruz.
1858.europe: London’s “Great Stink” from the sewage-filled Thames pushed Parliament to fund new sewers. In France, Bernadette Soubirous reported visions at Lourdes, and Napoleon III secretly agreed to back Piedmont against Austria.
1858.russia: In the Treaty of Aigun, Qing China ceded the north bank of the Amur to Russia. At home, noble committees set up by Alexander II debated how to free the serfs.
1858.mideast: The Ottoman Land Code required farmland to be registered, reshaping rural ownership. Ferdinand de Lesseps launched the Suez Canal Company, and Kisrawan peasants in Mount Lebanon rose against their lords.
1858.africa: John Hanning Speke reached the lake he named Victoria and declared it the Nile’s source. Moshoeshoe’s Basotho fought off the Orange Free State, and David Livingstone began his Zambezi expedition.
1858.india: After the 1857 uprising, the British Crown took over from the East India Company. Rani Lakshmibai of Jhansi died fighting in June, and the last Mughal emperor was exiled to Rangoon.
1858.china: Losing the Second Opium War, Qing China signed the Treaties of Tianjin, opening new ports. Japan signed a trade treaty with the US, and chief minister Ii Naosuke began purging critics.

1859.us: Edwin Drake struck oil in Titusville, Pennsylvania, in August. In October John Brown raided the federal arsenal at Harpers Ferry to spark a slave revolt, and was hanged in December.
1859.latam: From Veracruz, Benito Juárez issued the Reform Laws, nationalising Church property and creating civil marriage. In Argentina, the Confederation defeated Buenos Aires at Cepeda, pushing it to rejoin.
1859.europe: Charles Darwin published On the Origin of Species in November. France and Piedmont defeated Austria at Magenta and Solferino, where the carnage later moved Henry Dunant to found the Red Cross.
1859.russia: Imam Shamil, who had led North Caucasus resistance for 25 years, surrendered to Russian forces at Gunib. In St Petersburg, editorial commissions began drafting the emancipation of the serfs.
1859.mideast: Work on the Suez Canal began at the site of Port Said in April. In October, Spain declared war on Morocco over clashes near Ceuta.
1859.africa: David Livingstone’s expedition reached Lake Malawi in September. In Abeokuta, missionary Henry Townsend launched Iwe Irohin, often called Nigeria’s first newspaper, printed in Yoruba.
1859.india: Rebel leader Tantia Tope was betrayed, captured and hanged in April, ending the last campaign of 1857’s uprising. In Bengal, peasants began the Indigo Revolt against European planters.
1859.china: Qing guns at the Taku Forts drove off a British and French fleet in June. Japan opened Yokohama to foreign trade, and the Ansei Purge executed the teacher Yoshida Shōin.

1871.us: The Great Chicago Fire killed about 300 people in October, and the same night a forest fire at Peshtigo, Wisconsin, killed over 1,200. The New York Times exposed Boss Tweed’s corruption.
1871.latam: Brazil’s Law of Free Birth freed children born to enslaved mothers. Yellow fever killed about 14,000 people in Buenos Aires, and a liberal revolution took power in Guatemala.
1871.europe: Wilhelm I was proclaimed German emperor at Versailles in January, and defeated France gave up Alsace and part of Lorraine. Rome became the capital of united Italy.
1871.russia: A London conference let Russia station warships on the Black Sea again, undoing part of its Crimean War defeat. Dostoevsky began publishing Demons, inspired by the Nechayev affair.
1871.mideast: In Algeria, Cheikh El Mokrani led a large Kabyle revolt against French rule, which was crushed. Iran was in the grip of a devastating famine.
1871.africa: Henry Morton Stanley found David Livingstone at Ujiji on Lake Tanganyika. Diggers swarmed the diamond fields at what became Kimberley, and Britain annexed them as Griqualand West.
1871.india: The Criminal Tribes Act let British officials brand whole communities “criminal” by birth. In September, acting chief justice John Paxton Norman was stabbed to death in Calcutta.
1871.china: Japan abolished its feudal domains for prefectures, and the Iwakura Mission left to study the West. US marines stormed forts on Korea’s Ganghwa Island, and Russia occupied China’s Ili valley.

1876.us: Philadelphia hosted the Centennial Exhibition, and Lakota and Cheyenne warriors destroyed Custer’s command at the Little Bighorn. The Hayes–Tilden presidential election ended in bitter dispute.
1876.latam: Porfirio Díaz rebelled under the Plan of Tuxtepec and seized Mexico City in November, beginning decades in power. Brazil’s Emperor Pedro II toured the US and tried Bell’s telephone.
1876.europe: Ottoman forces crushed Bulgaria’s April Uprising, killing thousands, and Gladstone’s pamphlet on the “Bulgarian Horrors” stirred Britain. Wagner opened Bayreuth with the first complete Ring cycle.
1876.russia: Russia annexed the Central Asian Khanate of Kokand, and Russian volunteers under General Chernyayev fought for Serbia. Radicals of the new Land and Liberty group staged a protest in St Petersburg.
1876.mideast: The Ottoman Empire had three sultans in one year, and Abdul Hamid II proclaimed its first constitution in December. Bankrupt Egypt accepted a European-run debt commission.
1876.africa: Emperor Yohannes IV’s Ethiopian army routed an invading Egyptian force at Gura in March. In Brussels, Belgium’s King Leopold II hosted a conference that began his Congo ambitions.
1876.india: The monsoon failed in southern and western India, starting the Great Famine of 1876–78, which killed millions. Parliament gave Queen Victoria the title Empress of India.
1876.china: Japan forced Korea to open ports under the Treaty of Ganghwa, and banned samurai from wearing swords. China’s first railway opened near Shanghai, and drought began a terrible famine in the north.
